judgements.referenceQuote: President and CEO, Walmart, Inc.In officeFebruary 2014 – January 2026Preceded byMike DukeSucceeded byJohn Furner
judgements.evidenceQuote: McMillon is stepping down as Walmart president and CEO and has been succeeded by John Furner.
judgements.rationale: This claim covers the role (president and CEO), the retirement/step-down and the successor (John Furner), but no single dossier statement carries the full span: the February 2014 start ('CEO at Walmart since February 2014'), the January 2026 end ('Retired on January 31, 2026.') and the Furner succession appear only in separate claims, so the complete dated fact is only partially recovered.

judgements.referenceQuote: led the company's Sam's Club division, from 2005 to 2009, and Walmart International, from 2009 to 2013
judgements.evidenceQuote: led the company's Sam's Club division, from 2005 to 2009, and Walmart International, from 2009 to 2013.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states he led Sam's Club from 2005 to 2009 and Walmart International from 2009 to 2013, matching the reference fact's subjects, roles and dates exactly.

judgements.referenceQuote: He began his Walmart career in 1984 as an hourly associate
judgements.evidenceQuote: Began Walmart career in 1984 as an hourly associate.
judgements.rationale: The dossier gives the 1984 start and the hourly associate role, but omits that it was a summer job as a teenager unloading trucks in a distribution centre; other claims cover fragments (a summer warehouse job, unloading trucks) but none states the full fact with the date.

judgements.referenceQuote: It invested heavily in people by increasing wages, expanding parental leave and funding education opportunities. Walmart also lowered its prices, built a large eCommerce business and embraced technology to improve customer and associate experiences
judgements.evidenceQuote: McMillon accelerated investments in e-commerce and raised the minimum wage for workers.
judgements.rationale: The dossier supports some elements of the tenure record (wage increases, education opportunities via Live Better U, a large eCommerce business), but nowhere states the expanded parental leave, lowered prices, the shift to an omnichannel model, or that these come from Walmart's own account of his tenure, so only part of the fact is recovered.

judgements.referenceQuote: Doug also served on the boards of Business Roundtable and the Consumer Goods Forum
judgements.evidenceQuote: Served on the boards of Business Roundtable and the Consumer Goods Forum.
judgements.rationale: This claim recovers the Business Roundtable and Consumer Goods Forum board service, and a separate claim ('He also sits on the retailer's board of directors.') covers the Walmart board, but no single dossier statement combines all three board roles with the retirement timing of 31 January 2026.

judgements.referenceQuote: McMillon attended University of Arkansas, where he graduated with a  Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in accounting in 1989
judgements.evidenceQuote: Doug McMillon earned a BA in Accounting from the University of Arkansas in 1989 and an MBA from the University of Tulsa in 1991.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states an accounting degree from the University of Arkansas awarded in 1989 plus an MBA from the University of Tulsa, preserving the subjects, institutions and the 1989 date of the reference fact; the BA/BS wording difference does not change the fact.

judgements.referenceQuote: Doug McMillon is a lifelong merchant
judgements.evidenceQuote: But for most of his more than 40 years with the company, he was a merchant.
judgements.rationale: The dossier characterises him as a merchant, but it does not state that Walmart's own page describes him as 'a lifelong merchant' as a self-reported characterisation, so the attribution — the core of the reference fact — is only partly covered.

judgements.referenceQuote: McMillon was born in Memphis, Tennessee,[5] and grew up in Jonesboro, Arkansas,[6] the eldest of three children born to Laura and Morris McMillon, a dentist who served in Vietnam
judgements.rationale: The dossier contains nothing about his birth in Memphis, childhood in Jonesboro, Arkansas, being the eldest of three children, or the family's move to Bentonville when he was 16; the only Bentonville mention concerns a warehouse summer job, not his upbringing.
